# Safari DevTools

> Free, open-source (MIT) Chrome-style DevTools panel that runs inside any web page, in Safari, Chrome, Edge and on iPhone/iPad (including in-app WebViews). One dependency-free JavaScript file, plus browser extensions for Safari and Chrome. Current version: 1.5.2.

Safari DevTools gives Safari and iOS the debugging tools developers expect from Chrome DevTools, without a Mac, cable or Xcode. It is loaded into a page by a browser extension, a bookmarklet or a `<script>` tag, and shows a docked panel with: Console (source-mapped stack traces, autocomplete, live expressions, console.table), Elements (DOM through shadow roots, live CSS with design-token suggestions, grid/flex overlays, measure tool, Changes tab), Sources, Network (fetch/XHR/WebSocket/SSE, mock/block/delay rules, 3G/offline throttling, HAR export), Storage, Components (Angular signals, Lit, React; Redux/NgRx/Zustand time travel), Issues, Performance, Tokens, Assets, Audit, Accessibility (accessibility tree, tab-order overlay, focus tracker, contrast fixer using design tokens), Coverage (unused CSS and tokens), Snapshots (visual regression for components) and Device (emulation of dark mode, reduced motion, RTL, text size, pseudo-localisation; side-by-side iPhone/iPad preview).

It also has "Explain with Claude" for errors and one-click Jira bug reports (both run through a local relay with the user's own keys; sign-in codes and tokens are redacted), remote mode to stream an iPhone's console and network to a Mac over Wi-Fi, and an automation API exposed to Playwright, WebDriver, an HTTP API and an MCP server for AI agents.

Key facts:
- Install: Chrome/Edge extension (load unpacked), Safari extension (Add Temporary Extension, or build with Xcode), bookmarklet, or `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/biratdatta/safari-devtools@v1.5.2/standalone/safari-devtools.js"></script>`.
- Shortcuts: Ctrl+Shift+D or Alt+Shift+D toggles the panel; Ctrl+Shift+C or Alt+Shift+C picks an element; Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette.
- JavaScript API: `window.SafariDevTools` (show, hide, toggle, inspect) and `window.SafariDevTools.automation` (JSON methods such as logs, errors, network, har, mock, block, throttle, audit, a11yTree, tabOrder, contrast, coverage, emulate, snapshot, compareSnapshot, bugReport; call `help()` for the full list).
- Limits: it runs inside the page, so it cannot pause JavaScript at breakpoints, see HttpOnly cookies or browser-added headers, or read cross-origin stylesheets.
- Privacy: nothing leaves the page unless the user starts the optional relay for Claude or Jira.
- Languages of the website: English, Simplified Chinese (https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/zh/), Japanese (https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/ja/).

## Docs

- [Website](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/): overview, live demo, install steps, comparison and FAQ
- [Full documentation for LLMs](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/llms-full.txt): all READMEs in one Markdown file
- [Project README](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/README.md): features, comparison with Safari Web Inspector and Eruda/vConsole, changelog
- [Tool guide](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/standalone/README.md): every panel, remote mode, Claude and Jira setup, automation, shortcuts, limits
- [Bookmarklet](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/standalone/bookmarklet.md): use it where extensions are not allowed
- [Chrome extension](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/chrome-extension/README.md): install and troubleshooting for Chrome and Edge
- [Safari extension](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/extension/README.md): install with Safari or Xcode

## Automation and AI agents

- [Playwright fixture](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/standalone/playwright/safari-devtools.fixture.ts): typed `devtools` fixture for WebKit and Chromium tests
- [MCP server](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/standalone/remote/mcp.js): tools such as get_console, get_network, run_js, audit_page, inspect_element, mock_request, accessibility_tree, check_contrast, css_coverage, emulate, compare_snapshot, bug_report, explain_error_context
- [Relay and HTTP API](https://github.com/biratdatta/safari-devtools/blob/main/standalone/remote/relay.js): /api/devices, /api/logs, /api/network, /api/eval, /api/call; optional /ai/explain and /jira/create

## Comparisons

- [Safari DevTools vs Safari Web Inspector](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/compare/safari-web-inspector/): Safari's Web Inspector needs a Mac and a cable or pairing. Safari DevTools runs inside the page. When to use each, and what each can't do.
- [Safari DevTools vs Eruda](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/compare/eruda/): Eruda and Safari DevTools both put a console inside the page. How they differ on source maps, request mocking, accessibility, Redux and setup.
- [Safari DevTools vs vConsole](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/compare/vconsole/): vConsole is Tencent's lightweight in-page console, popular in WeChat. How it compares with Safari DevTools for debugging iPhone and mobile web pages.
- [Safari DevTools vs Chrome DevTools](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/compare/chrome-devtools/): Chrome DevTools is the gold standard on desktop and Android but can't attach to iPhone. Where Safari DevTools fits, and what Chrome still does better.
- [Eruda alternatives for mobile debugging](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/compare/eruda-alternatives/): The main alternatives to Eruda for debugging pages on iPhone and Android: Safari DevTools, vConsole, Safari Web Inspector and Chrome remote debugging.

## Guides and how-tos

- [How to see console logs on iPhone without a Mac](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/iphone-console-without-mac/): Three ways to read console logs and errors from Safari on iPhone without a Mac or cable: a bookmarklet, a script tag, or remote mode over Wi-Fi.
- [How to debug Safari on iPhone: every method compared](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/debug-safari-on-iphone/): All the ways to debug a web page in Safari on iPhone and iPad: Web Inspector, an in-page panel, remote mode and automated tests, with what each needs.
- [How to debug WKWebView and in-app browsers on iOS](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/debug-ios-webviews/): Debug web content inside iOS apps: make WKWebView inspectable, or inject an in-page DevTools panel. Tips for React Native, Capacitor and Android too.
- [How to mock, block and slow down API calls in the browser](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/mock-api-in-browser/): Test error states, empty states and slow networks without a proxy: mock responses, block requests and throttle to 3G from an in-page DevTools panel.
- [Accessibility testing in Safari: tree, tab order and contrast](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/safari-accessibility-testing/): Check what VoiceOver gets, walk the tab order, catch focus escaping dialogs and fix low-contrast text with colours from your design tokens, in Safari.
- [Redux DevTools in Safari (and NgRx, Zustand)](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/redux-devtools-safari/): Safari has no Redux DevTools extension. Safari DevTools provides the same API, so Redux Toolkit, NgRx and Zustand connect, with an action log and time travel.
- [Safari-only CSS bugs on iPhone, and how to fix them](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/safari-css-bugs/): The iPhone Safari layout bugs behind most bug reports: input zoom, 100vh, safe areas, sticky inside overflow, fixed inside transforms, autoplay and tap targets.
- [Debugging web components and shadow DOM in Safari](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/learn/debug-shadow-dom-safari/): Inspect shadow roots, slots, ::part() hooks and the CSS variables a web component reads, edit properties live, and search across shadow boundaries.

## Setup

- [Install Safari DevTools in Chrome and Edge](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/guides/install-chrome/): Install the Safari DevTools extension in Chrome, Edge, Brave or Arc in about a minute, open it with Alt+Shift+D, and fix common problems.
- [Install Safari DevTools in Safari on Mac](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/guides/install-safari/): Add the Safari DevTools extension to Safari as a temporary extension in a minute, or build it once with Xcode to keep it installed. Includes troubleshooting.
- [Remote mode: debug an iPhone from your computer over Wi-Fi](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/guides/remote-iphone/): Stream an iPhone page's console and network to your computer and run JavaScript on the phone with a small Node relay. No cable or Xcode; works on Windows.
- [Set up "Explain with Claude" and Jira bug reports](https://devtools.biratdatta.tech/guides/claude-and-jira/): Turn on AI error explanations with Claude and one-click Jira bug reports, using a local relay that keeps your API key and Jira token on your machine.
